---
title: "05 - Bivariate analyses and descriptive figures"
output: html_document
---

**Purpose.** Produces descriptive figures of the GROA-AF carbon data (carbon and age distributions, carbon vs. system age, carbon by agroforestry category and ecoregion) and fits bivariate models of each carbon pool (AGC, BGC, ΔSOC and their annual change rates) against each candidate predictor. Continuous predictors use simple linear regression; binary and categorical predictors use one-way linear models with effect (sum-to-zero) contrasts against the grand mean. The model summaries feed the predictor summary table (notebook 07) and the random forest analysis (notebook 10).

**Inputs.** (all produced by notebook 04)

- `output/data/{agc,bgc,soc}_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx`
- `output/data/{agc,bgc,soc}_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx`

**Outputs.**

- `output/figures/age_density.png`
- `output/figures/c_density_by_age_panel.png`
- `output/figures/c_by_age_scatter_panel.png`
- `output/figures/c_by_cat_violin_panel.png`
- `output/figures/c_by_ecoreg_violin_panel.png`
- `output/tables/bivariate_model_summaries.xlsx` (one sheet per predictor type, plus a Notes sheet)
- `output/tables/bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv` (used by notebooks 06 and 09)


```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(skimr)
library(ggpmisc)
library(patchwork)
library(forcats)
library(broom)
library(emmeans)
```

Load the final analysis datasets (outliers removed) for each carbon pool, produced by notebook 05.
```{r load-data}
agc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
agc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "agc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
bgc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
bgc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "bgc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
soc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
soc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "soc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
```


## Options and labels

Analysis options, agroforestry category lookups, and plot/table labels.
```{r options}
# Select whether to use SOC stock or delta from baseline
use_soc_delta <- T

af_cats <- c('AC', 'BP', 'COP', 'FAL', 'FOD', 'MS', 'OTH_AF', 'PAR', 'RB', 'ROT', 'SA', 'SP', 'SPC', 'TMC', 'WL')

af_cat_labels <- c('AC' = "Alley cropping", 
                   'BP' = 'Boundary planting', 
                   'COP' = 'Coppice', 
                   'FAL' = 'Fallows', 
                   'FOD' = 'Fodder bank',
                   'MS' = 'Multistrata', 
                   'OTH_AF' = 'Other Agroforestry',
                   'PAR' = 'Parklands', 
                   'RB' = 'Riparian Buffer', 
                   'ROT' = 'Rotational', 
                   'SA' = 'Silvoarable', 
                   'SP' = 'Silvopasture', 
                   'SPC' = 'Shaded perennial',
                   'TMC' = 'Tree monocrop', 
                   'WL' = 'Woodlot')

c_data_names <- c('agc', 'bgc', 'soc', 'agc_change', 'bgc_change', 'soc_change')
c_data_labels <- c('agc' = "AGC", 'bgc' = "BGC", 'soc' = expression(Delta * "SOC"), 'agc_change' = "AGC change", 'bgc_change' = "BGC change", 'soc_change' = expression(Delta * "SOC change"))

# Plain-text labels for the "c_pool" column in output tables (not plotmath
# expressions like c_data_labels). SOC is labeled "\u0394SOC" when
# use_soc_delta is selected, since c_t_ha is then the delta from baseline.
c_pool_labels <- c('agc' = "AGC",
                    'bgc' = "BGC",
                    'soc' = if (use_soc_delta) "\u0394SOC" else "SOC",
                    'agc_change' = "AGC change",
                    'bgc_change' = "BGC change",
                    'soc_change' = "\u0394SOC change")
dep_var_labels <- c('c_t_ha' = expression(C~stock~(Mg~ha^{-1})), 'c_t_ha_yr' = expression(C~change~(Mg~ha^{-1}~yr^{-1})))
```


If `use_soc_delta` is TRUE, replace SOC stock (`c_t_ha`) with the AF-minus-control delta (`c_t_ha_delta`) so downstream code needs no changes.
```{r soc-delta}
if (use_soc_delta) {
  soc_df <- soc_df %>%
    mutate(c_t_ha = c_t_ha_delta) %>%
    select(-c_t_ha_delta)
}
```

## Descriptive figures


Distribution of system age across all AGC, BGC and SOC observations.
```{r age-density}
comb_df <- agc_df %>% bind_rows(bgc_df) %>% bind_rows(soc_df)

mean_age <- mean(comb_df$age)
median_age <- median(comb_df$age)
max_age <- max(comb_df$age)

plot_obj <- comb_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age)) +
  geom_density(fill = "deepskyblue", color = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_age, color = "deepskyblue4", linetype = "dashed", size = .75) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_age, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed", size = .75) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = max_age, color = "black", linetype = "dashed", size = .75) +
  xlim(0, max_age) +
  labs(x = "System age at measurement",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),  # removes y-axis numbers
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), # optional: removes y-axis ticks
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), # remove major y grid lines
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),  # remove minor y grid lines
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())


# Get max y-axis value from histogram to position the label
gg_data <- ggplot_build(plot_obj)$data[[1]]
max_y <- max(gg_data$y)
y_range <- max(gg_data$y) - min(gg_data$y)
x_range <- max(gg_data$x) - min(gg_data$x)

plot_obj <- plot_obj +
  annotate("label", x = mean_age + x_range * .01, y = max_y - y_range * .4, label = paste0("Mean age = ", round(mean_age, 2)),
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0, color = "deepskyblue4", fill = "white", size = 3) +
  annotate("label", x = median_age + x_range * .01, y = max_y - y_range * .3, label = paste0("Median age = ", round(median_age, 2)),
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0, color = "darkred", fill = "white", size = 3) +
  annotate("label", x = max_age * .99, y = max_y - y_range * .5, label = paste0("Max age = ", round(max_age, 2)),
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, color = "black", fill = "white", size = 3)

print(plot_obj)
ggsave(here("output", "figures", "age_density.png"), width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 600)
```

```{r c-density-by-age, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
for (c_data_name in c_data_names_stock) {

  var_name <- 'c_t_ha'

  my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))

  for (i in 1:(length(age_ranges) - 1)) {

    my_c_df_my_age <- my_c_df %>% filter(!!sym(age_var_name) > age_ranges[i],
                                         !!sym(age_var_name) <= age_ranges[i+1])

    mean <- mean(my_c_df_my_age[[var_name]])

      ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(var_name))) +

      labs(x = dep_var_labels[var_name],

      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

            panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),  # remove minor y grid lines

    # Get axis values from histogram to position the label
```

## Bivariate analyses

### Continuous predictors

Scatter plots with OLS fits, and one simple linear regression per carbon pool x predictor.
```{r cont-vars, fig.height=10, fig.width=7}
cont_var_model_summary_table <- tibble()

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }

  my_cont_vars <- cont_vars[cont_vars %in% colnames(get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')))]

  plot_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in my_cont_vars) {

    my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
    n_total <- nrow(my_c_df)

    plot_obj <- my_c_df %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(cont_var), y = !!sym(dep_var_name))) +
      geom_point(size = .5) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, color = "blue", linewidth = .5) +
      stat_poly_eq(
        formula = y ~ x,
        aes(label = paste(..eq.label.., ..rr.label.., ..p.value.label.., sep = "~~~")),
        parse = TRUE,
        size = 2.2,
        label.x = 'right',
        label.y = 'top'
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

    plot_list[[cont_var]] <- plot_obj


    model <- lm(reformulate(cont_var, response = dep_var_name), data = my_c_df)

    # tidy the output
    tidy_model <- tidy(model)

    # Flag models fit on < 10% of the pool's full sample (small, likely
    # non-random subsample -- see predictor_summary_table footnote)
    n_model <- nobs(model)
    pct_n <- round(100 * n_model / n_total, 1)

    table_dat <- tidy_model %>%
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
      mutate(
        c_pool = c_pool_labels[[c_data_name]],
        dependent_var = dep_var_name,
        independent_var = term,
        n = n_model,
        low_n = pct_n < 10,
        significance = case_when(
          p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
          p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
          p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
          TRUE            ~ ""
        )
      ) %>%
      bind_cols(tibble(r.squared = summary(model)$r.squared)) %>%
      dplyr::select(c_pool, independent_var, dependent_var, estimate, std.error, statistic, r.squared, p.value, significance, n, low_n)

    cont_var_model_summary_table <- cont_var_model_summary_table %>% bind_rows(table_dat)


  }

  combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 3, axis_titles = 'collect') +
    plot_annotation(title = c_data_name)

  suppressWarnings(print(combined_plot))
}
```

### Binary predictors

Management practices and plant traits. Each level is compared to the grand mean with effect contrasts; only the `= 1` row is kept.
```{r bin-vars, fig.height=10, fig.width=7}
bin_var_model_summary_table <- tibble()

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }

  plot_list <- list()

  my_bin_vars <- bin_vars[bin_vars %in% colnames(get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')))] # all bin vars


  for (bin_var in my_bin_vars) {
    my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
    n_total <- nrow(my_c_df)
    my_c_df[[bin_var]] <- factor(my_c_df[[bin_var]])

    plot_obj <- my_c_df %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(bin_var), y = !!sym(dep_var_name))) +
      geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, shape = 16, color = 'blue', size = .5) +
      geom_boxplot(fill = "white", alpha = .5, color = "black", outliers = F) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

    plot_list[[bin_var]] <- plot_obj

    # use effect coding (sum to zero contrasts) to compare each group to the grand mean

    # Set contrasts globally or for the variable
    contrasts(my_c_df[[bin_var]]) <- contr.sum(length(levels(my_c_df[[bin_var]])))

    model <- lm(reformulate(bin_var, response = dep_var_name), data = my_c_df)

    # Estimated marginal means (aka least square means)
    em <- emmeans(model, specs = bin_var)

    # Compare each category to the grand mean
    grand_mean <- mean(my_c_df[[dep_var_name]])
    tests <- contrast(em, method = "eff")  # effect coding comparisons

    # Tidy output
    tidy_tests <- tidy(tests)

    # Flag models fit on < 10% of the pool's full sample (small, likely
    # non-random subsample -- see predictor_summary_table footnote)
    n_model <- nobs(model)
    pct_n <- round(100 * n_model / n_total, 1)

    table_dat <- tidy_tests %>%
      mutate(
        c_pool = c_pool_labels[[c_data_name]],
        dependent_var = dep_var_name,
        independent_var = bin_var,
        category = str_replace(contrast, ' effect', ''),
        p.value = adj.p.value,
        n = n_model,
        low_n = pct_n < 10,
        significance = case_when(
          p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
          p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
          p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
          TRUE            ~ ""
        )
      ) %>%
      bind_cols(tibble(r.squared = summary(model)$r.squared)) %>%
      dplyr::select(c_pool, independent_var, category, dependent_var, estimate, std.error, statistic, r.squared, p.value, significance, n, low_n)

    table_dat <- table_dat %>%
      filter(!grepl("0", category)) %>%
      mutate(category = str_replace(category, "1", " = 1"))

    bin_var_model_summary_table <- bin_var_model_summary_table %>% bind_rows(table_dat)
  }

  combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2, axis_titles = 'collect') +
    plot_annotation(title = c_data_name)

  suppressWarnings(print(combined_plot))

}
```


### Categorical predictors (mutually exclusive factors)

Each model reports a full-model F-test row plus effect contrasts of each category vs. the grand mean (emmeans-adjusted p-values).

Agroforestry category.
```{r af-cat, fig.height=4, fig.width=7}
af_cat_model_summary_table <- tibble()

plot_list <- list()

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else {
    dep_var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }

  my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
  n_total <- nrow(my_c_df)

  my_c_df <- my_c_df %>%
    filter(af_cat %in% af_cats)

  my_c_df <- my_c_df %>%
    mutate(af_cat = af_cat_labels[af_cat]) %>%
    mutate(af_cat = str_replace_all(af_cat, ' ' , '\n')) %>%
    mutate(af_cat = factor(af_cat)) %>%
    mutate(af_cat = fct_reorder(af_cat, !!sym(dep_var_name), .fun = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), .desc = TRUE))


  medians_df <- my_c_df %>%
    group_by(af_cat) %>%
    summarise(median_val = median(!!sym(dep_var_name), na.rm = TRUE))


  plot_obj <- my_c_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(af_cat, !!sym(dep_var_name), FUN = function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE), decreasing = T), 
               y = !!sym(dep_var_name))) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, shape = 16, color = 'deepskyblue4', size = .4, stroke = 0) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "gray20") +
    stat_summary(fun = function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 
                 geom = "crossbar", width = .4, linewidth = .2, 
                 color = "deeppink4") +
    geom_label(
      data = medians_df,
      aes(
        x = af_cat,
        y = median_val,
        label = sprintf("%.1f", median_val)
      ),
      nudge_x = 0.45,
      fill = alpha("white", 0.8),   # semi‑transparent background
      label.size = 0,               # **removes border**
      label.padding = unit(0.02, "lines"),
      color = "deeppink4",               # text color only
      size = 2.25,
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) +
    labs(title = c_data_labels[c_data_name], x = 'Agroforestry category', y = dep_var_labels[dep_var_name]) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
    )

  plot_list[[c_data_name]] <- plot_obj


  # use effect coding (sum to zero contrasts) to compare each group to the grand mean

  # Set contrasts globally or for the variable
  contrasts(my_c_df$af_cat) <- contr.sum(length(levels(my_c_df$af_cat)))

  model <- lm(reformulate('af_cat', response = dep_var_name), data = my_c_df)

  # Estimated marginal means (aka least square means)
  em <- emmeans(model, ~ af_cat)

  # Compare each category to the grand mean
  grand_mean <- mean(my_c_df[[dep_var_name]])
  tests <- contrast(em, method = "eff")  # effect coding comparisons

  # Tidy output
  tidy_tests <- tidy(tests)

  model_sum <- summary(model)
  fs <- model_sum$fstatistic
  model_p <- pf(fs[1], fs[2], fs[3], lower.tail = FALSE)

  # Flag models fit on < 10% of the pool's full sample (small, likely
  # non-random subsample -- see predictor_summary_table footnote)
  n_model <- nobs(model)
  pct_n <- round(100 * n_model / n_total, 1)

  full_model_row <- tibble(
    c_pool        = c_pool_labels[[c_data_name]],
    independent_var = 'af_cat',
    category      = 'Full model',
    dependent_var = dep_var_name,
    estimate      = NA_real_,
    std.error     = NA_real_,
    statistic     = NA_real_,
    r.squared     = model_sum$r.squared,
    p.value       = model_p,
    n             = n_model,
    low_n         = pct_n < 10,
    significance  = case_when(
      model_p < 0.001 ~ "***",
      model_p < 0.01  ~ "**",
      model_p < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )

  category_rows <- tidy_tests %>%
    mutate(
      c_pool = c_pool_labels[[c_data_name]],
      dependent_var = dep_var_name,
      independent_var = 'af_cat',
      category = str_replace(contrast, ' effect', ''),
      p.value = adj.p.value,
      r.squared = NA_real_,
      n = n_model,
      low_n = pct_n < 10,
      significance = case_when(
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE            ~ ""
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(c_pool, independent_var, category, dependent_var, estimate, std.error, statistic, r.squared, p.value, significance, n, low_n)

  table_dat <- bind_rows(full_model_row, category_rows)

  af_cat_model_summary_table <- af_cat_model_summary_table %>% bind_rows(table_dat)

}

combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list[c(1,3)], ncol = 1, axes = 'collect', axis_titles = 'collect')
suppressWarnings(print(combined_plot))
```

### Categorical predictors derived from dummy variables

Drop the original categorical columns (`ctrl_cat`, `prior_land_use`, `soil_texture_class`) the dummies were built from, so they are not caught by the `prior_`/`ctrl_`/`soil_tex_` prefix matching below.
```{r drop-cat-cols}
for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))

  if (c_data_name == 'soc' || c_data_name == 'soc_change') {
    my_c_df <- my_c_df %>%
      select(-c(ctrl_cat, prior_land_use, soil_texture_class))
  } else {
    my_c_df <- my_c_df %>%
      select(-c(prior_land_use, soil_texture_class))
  }
  assign(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'), my_c_df)
}
```


Prior land use (category reconstructed from the `prior_*` dummies, taking the largest value per row).
```{r prior-cat}
prior_cat_model_summary_table <- tibble()

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {

    mutate(across(all_of(prior_cols), ~ifelse(is.na(.), 0, .))) %>%
    rowwise() %>%

      row_vals <- c_across(all_of(prior_cols))
      max_idx <- which.max(row_vals)
```

## Write model summary tables

Combine all bivariate model summaries into one workbook (one sheet per predictor type) and a long CSV used by notebooks 06 and 10.
```{r write-summaries}
model_summary_df_names <- c('cont_var_model_summary_table',
                            'bin_var_model_summary_table',
                            'af_cat_model_summary_table',
                            'audebert_reg_model_summary_table',
                            'prior_cat_model_summary_table',
                            'ctrl_cat_model_summary_table',
                            'soil_tex_cat_model_summary_table')

# Format numbers: round to 2 dp, replace non-zero values that round to 0.00 with "<0.01"
fmt_num <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_,
    ifelse(round(x, 2) == 0 & x != 0, "<0.01",
           sprintf("%.2f", x)))
}

# Caveat footnote for models fit on < 10% of the pool's full sample
low_n_footnote <- "\u2020 n represents less than 10% of the full sample for that carbon pool; the estimate is based on a small, likely non-random subsample of studies (predictors like management practices are only reported by a handful of studies) and should be interpreted with caution."

format_summary_table <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    # Ensure category follows independent_var
    relocate(any_of("category"), .after = independent_var) %>%
    # Strip emmeans-added parentheses around category names (caused by slashes in names)
    mutate(across(any_of("category"), ~str_replace(., "^\\((.*)\\)$", "\\1"))) %>%
    # Round all numeric columns (n/low_n handled separately below)
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !any_of(c("n")), fmt_num)) %>%
    # Demarcate low-n rows (< 10% of pool's full sample) with a dagger
    # Use a dagger (not "*") so low-n rows aren't confused with the sig. column
    mutate(n = if_else(low_n, paste0(n, "\u2020"), as.character(n))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-low_n)
}

# Create a new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

for (name in model_summary_df_names) {
  short_name <- str_replace(name, '_model_summary_table', '')
  addWorksheet(wb, short_name)
  writeData(wb, short_name, get(name) |> format_summary_table())
}

# Footnote sheet with the low-n caveat
addWorksheet(wb, "Notes")
writeData(wb, "Notes", low_n_footnote)

# Save workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, here("output", "tables", "bivariate_model_summaries.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)

# Save combined long CSV
mget(model_summary_df_names) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  format_summary_table() %>%
  write_csv(here("output", "tables", "bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv"))
```
